notes: The Oracle Fund recipient is fixed to 0x788C311500FD3C15b8e44d6e2935fe7fF13E674b in the manifest and constructor. Constructor order remains (IPoolManager poolManager_, address panic_, address oracleFund_); a zero recipient reverts with ZeroAddress and any other recipient reverts with InvalidOracleFund. The hook accepts the listed static LP fee 12500. It binds the first pool containing PANIC, rejects dynamic fees and subsequent pools, and supports either ERC-20 currency ordering. Tick spacing 250 and initial sqrtPriceX96 2^96 follow the deployment test; the initial price means one raw currency1 unit per raw currency0 unit, without adjusting for paired-token decimals. The manifest selects the requested ERC-20 pair; the repository deployment script instead initializes a native-ETH pool and does not implement this manifest's pool selection. Permissions match getHookPermissions, with address mask 0x35cf. Enabled callbacks and unlockCallback accept only PoolManager. afterAddLiquidity/afterRemoveLiquidity (with return deltas) make a position that was added to in the current block forfeit the fees it collects by being touched again in that block; the forfeited fees are donated to the remaining in-range liquidity (with none left, the paired part waits in the donation bucket and PANIC goes to the dead address), so same-transaction JIT liquidity cannot recapture the LP share of a hook fee. LPs who add and collect in the same block lose those same-block fees. The implementation uses Cancun transient storage and has no owner, pause, upgrade or setters for economic constants. Reference: a 3600-second geometric TWAP from cumulative ticks, at most one pre-first-swap observation per block; the initialization tick fills prelaunch history. Buys use pre-buy drawdown: 0% below 5%, 1% at or above 5%. Sells use post-sell drawdown: 2% below 5%, 10% from 5% to below 15%, 20% from 15% to below 30%, 30% from 30%. Fees are in the paired currency, additional to the 1.25% LP fee, and accrue as ERC-6909 claims. Exact-input buys charge through beforeSwap return delta; exact-output buys charge paired input through afterSwap return delta. Exact-input sells charge paired output through afterSwap; exact-output sells revert, and fee-bearing exact-input buys that would fill only partially (binding sqrtPriceLimitX96) revert: integrators must route sells exact-input and price-limited dip buys exact-output. Each fee assigns floor(30%) to LPs, floor(10%) to burning, and the remainder to the Oracle Fund, totaling 100% without unallocated split dust. Anyone can call claimOracleFund to the immutable recipient, donateToLiquidityProviders via PoolManager.donate, or buybackAndBurn. Buybacks spend at most 1000000000000000000 paired-token minor units per call (or a smaller caller limit), send purchased PANIC directly to 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD, restore unspent budget, and revert below ceil(98%) of the unrounded reference-implied output. Splitting a sell across fee tiers may pay less total hook tax because early pieces land at lower tiers. This is intended and accepted; the anti-splitting tests have been removed and no per-wallet tracking is added. PoolManager skips callbacks for the hook's own buyback swaps, so those swaps pay no hook fee. These implementation limitations require review; this manifest does not resolve them.
